title_candidates: Claude Code auto mode becomes the default on August 14
summary: Claude Code will default new Pro, Max, and Team sessions to auto mode, trading repeated approval prompts for background safety checks.

primary_source.title: Auto mode is now the default in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team plans
primary_source.author: Anthropic
key_facts: New sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans move to auto mode on August 14.
Pinned defaults remain unchanged and Enterprise or cloud-platform deployments remain opt-in initially.
A study of 1,053 paid testers found humans blocked 13.6% of dangerous prompts while auto mode blocked 89%.
The classifier reduces approval fatigue but did not block every dangerous test command.

supporting_sources.title: Choose a permission mode
key_facts: The official docs explain mode selection, protected paths, background checks, and fallback to manual approval.

supporting_sources.title: Auto mode is now the default in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team plans
key_facts: Simon Willison notes that the remaining failures still justify isolating valuable data and tools.

prerequisites: A Claude Pro, Max, or Team account
A disposable or non-sensitive sample project

steps.instruction: Check the permission mode in a fresh session and use Manual or Plan for sensitive work.
Test auto mode only in a recoverable project with explicit network, credential, deletion, and folder boundaries.
